title: Finding health care in Germany
intro: This article concerns services in Germany, not the rules in Moldova or every European country. Knowing where to ask for routine, urgent and emergency care can reduce delays and unnecessary journeys.

sections.heading: Routine care and referrals
paragraphs: For ongoing symptoms, prescriptions and prevention, a general practice is often a useful starting point. Ask whether it accepts your insurance and whether you need an appointment; requirements for specialist referrals depend on the service and insurance arrangements.

sections.heading: Prepare for the appointment
paragraphs: Bring your insurance information, medicine list, relevant records and the questions that matter most. Explain communication or access needs in advance. An interpreter can help; availability and payment should be clarified rather than assuming every practice provides translation.

sections.heading: Urgent care outside normal hours
paragraphs: When practices are closed and a problem cannot wait but is not life-threatening, Germany’s on-call medical service can advise through 116117. Its telephone service is provided in German; ask about accessible alternatives if language or hearing makes calling difficult.

sections.heading: Life-threatening emergencies
paragraphs: For life-threatening illness, severe breathing difficulty, suspected stroke or collapse, call 112. Describe the location and symptoms and follow instructions. Do not postpone emergency help while searching for insurance documents or a routine appointment.

sections.heading: Results, medicines and costs
paragraphs: Before leaving a consultation, clarify the plan, follow-up and how results will arrive. Medicines are obtained from pharmacies; ask about instructions and possible charges. These pathways do not determine individual coverage, so clarify non-urgent costs with the practice and insurer.

examples.title: A practical example
examples.text: In this hypothetical example, Mira develops a painful problem when her practice is closed. She uses the on-call route because it cannot wait, while understanding that life-threatening symptoms need emergency services.

examples.title: Another practical example
examples.text: In this hypothetical example, Arben brings a medicine list and requests language support before a planned visit. He checks how to receive results rather than assuming silence means everything is normal.

questions: Which service should I use for my situation?
What communication support can be arranged?
How will I receive results and follow-up instructions?
